title: Converge call-level deadlines, backoff curves, and idempotency semantics across SDKs and runtime
creator: Maya Patel
description: Standardize retry, timeout, and backoff behaviour across service runtimes and official SDKs; define a forward-compatible idempotency key format and hedged request contract so clients and server can coordinate duplicates suppression and load-shedding. This ticket covers the spec, cross-team alignment, SDK implementations, runtime hooks, and a staged rollout plan.
background: We currently have several interoperability problems: SDKs implement different backoff curves and default deadlines, runtime endpoints vary in duplicate suppression behaviour, and there is no versioned idempotency key format. These differences cause unfair retry amplification, inconsistent hedging outcomes, and difficulty diagnosing duplicate-response incidents. This work unifies policy so SLOs and cost projections are predictable across customers.
goals: 1) Produce a clear resilience contract document (client + server) describing deadlines, backoff curves with jitter, hedging semantics, and idempotency key format/versioning. 2) Implement the minimal runtime support (headers + duplicate suppression window + metrics). 3) Add the policy primitives to official SDKs (Go/Node/Python/Java). 4) Deploy via canaries and measure impact on latency P50/P95, retry volume, and duplicate-response rate.
non_goals: We will not replace per-route custom retry tuning here; teams may opt into default policy or supply per-route overrides. This ticket does not implement per-customer billing changes or chargeback rules.
success_metrics: client_retry_count: -30% target within 4 weeks of rollout
hedged_success_ratio: >= 95% of hedged wins without producing duplicate observable responses
p95-latency: not increased by more than 5% during steady-state
acceptance_criteria: Contract doc published in Confluence and approved by Runtime, SDK, and Platform PMs
Runtime accepts X-Hedge-Token and X-Idemp-Key headers and exposes duplicate_response_rate metric
SDKs expose a single BackoffPolicy and HedgePolicy with sane defaults and a migration guide
Canary customers (5% traffic) show stable SLOs and reduced retry amplification
Rollout feature flag allows opt-in per-customer and immediate rollback
work_items: Add header parsing + suppression KV window to runtime
SDK: new BackoffPolicy/hedging primitives + docs + examples
Integration tests for duplicate suppression and hedged-success semantics
Full rollout and deprecation schedule for legacy idempotency formats
notes_and_discussion: Design choices discussed with SDK leads: prefer a single canonical BackoffPolicy implementation exported by SDKs and avoid per-language curve divergence. Runtime team proposes a duplicate suppression window of 45s for non-streaming text generation requests; SDK team recommended 60s to accommodate slow networks — compromise set at 50s. Hedging contract introduces an optional X-Hedge-Token header; if present the runtime will dedupe downstream effectful calls for token-matched hedges within suppression window.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Spec and tests (2 weeks). Phase B: Runtime header + suppression + metrics (2 sprints). Phase C: SDK surface changes and test harness (Go/Node/Python/Java) (3 sprints). Phase D: Canary + measure (1 sprint). Phase E: Gradual rollout + deprecation of legacy modes (4 weeks). Key engineering tasks: 1) implement suppression token storage in runtime (use existing KV cache with TTL), 2) add backoff governor module in SDKs with curve 'truncated-exponential with bounded full jitter (alpha=0.3)', 3) hedged request flow: SDK sends primary request then spawns a hedged attempt at delay H (computed from observed latency percentile), 4) server dedups effects on matching X-Idemp-Key and X-Hedge-Token pairs.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary (10% developer traffic) with feature flag. 2) External canary: 5% customer traffic (select low-risk accounts). 3) Expand to 25% while verifying metrics. 4) Full rollout. Provide immediate rollback flag per route. Communicate SDK changes with a 6-week migration window and publish migration guide.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK backoff math and hedging timers. Integration tests simulating: high tail latency, server-side failures, and duplicate-suppression behavior. Chaos tests for network partitions and multi-region failover to ensure hedging doesn't exponentially amplify cross-region traffic. Load test to measure token cost delta and retry amplification under our default policy.
risks: Duplicate suppression may accidentally hide legitimate retries if idempotency keys are malformed by clients
Hedging can increase egress across regions if hedge routing is misconfigured
Older SDKs without the new headers may continue to retry aggressively—requires deprecation plan
Incorrect suppression TTL can increase stale suppression window causing lost actions for legitimate retries
